390.who: A parent with two kids, ages 3 and 7, in Colorado
390.answerText: You are paid $38,000 a year. You keep $84,371. More pay does not add to that until you are paid $45,000: a raise of $7,000.
390.caption: The side numbers start at $20,000, not at $0, so the drops are easy to see. From $119,000 up, more pay always adds to what you keep. These are estimates. They use the rules for 2026 in Colorado.
390.readout: Paid $38,000 a year, you keep $84,371. This pay is inside your flat stretch.
390.source: We could not get your exact numbers right now. These are numbers for a family like yours in your state.Try againSource: HotGap, from PolicyEngine 2.5.0 with 2026 rules. Rent: HUD Fair Market Rents, FY2026. Child care price: county 2015, grown to 2026 dollars. Sweep of 2026-09-16. Money kept is what is left after taxes and health-plan premiums.
steps: $7,000Cash help ends. It is called TANF cash assistance. You keep about $3,900 less.
$27,000Your tax breaks get smaller here. You keep about $600 less.
$38,000Your own free state health plan ends. It is called Medicaid. Then help paying for health insurance starts. It is called the Premium tax credit. You keep about $200 less.
$41,000Your kids' free state health plan would end. It is called Medicaid. Then a health plan for kids would start. It is called CHIP.
$42,000Your tax breaks would get smaller here. You would keep about $300 less.
$47,000Your tax breaks would get smaller here. You would keep about $400 less.
$52,000Your tax breaks would get smaller here. You would keep about $800 less.

$54,000Food help would end. It is called SNAP. Food help for moms and babies would end. It is called WIC. Some goes on until $55,000: $713 of food help and $181 of food help for moms and babies. You would keep about $2,400 less.
$55,000Child care help would end. It is called the CCDF child care subsidy. You would keep about $25,400 less. This is the biggest drop.
$59,000A tax break for workers would end. It is called the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC).
$61,000Your tax breaks would get smaller here. You would keep about $900 less.
$73,000A health plan for kids would end. It is called CHIP. Then help paying for health insurance would start. It is called the Premium tax credit.
$107,000Help paying for health insurance would end. It is called the Premium tax credit. You would keep about $3,800 less.
assumed: Rent$1,735 a month. The usual rent in El Paso County, the county we use for Colorado.
Child care$2,773 a month for two kids. The usual price of day care there.

Help you getFood help (SNAP), cash help (TANF cash assistance), a free state health plan (Medicaid), food help for moms and babies (WIC) and child care help (CCDF child care subsidy). We count each as if you get it.
Not countedHousing help (Housing voucher) and free early learning (Head Start). We count them as if you do not get them.
YouAge 30. A U.S. citizen. No one in the home has a disability.
SavingsNone. No child support, SSDI or unemployment pay.
HoursNot used. You gave your pay by the year.
390.reach: About 4 in 10 parents like you in Colorado are paid $38,000 a year or less. The count could be off by a few thousand dollars either way.
390.reachSource: From U.S. Census Bureau ACS 2024 1-Year public-use microdata, grown to 2026 dollars. 393 households in this cell; the margin at this point is about $8,000.
390.hours: Colorado's lowest legal pay is $15.16 an hour. Full-time work at that pay is about $31,500 a year.
